topics.topic: Backup encryption format, key fingerprint construction, and authentication of readable metadata
questions: What exact authenticated-encryption format is used, and are the instant, release, audit sequence and key digest cryptographically authenticated as part of that backup?

Which authenticated-encryption construction, nonce-generation rule, key derivation or interpretation, and digest algorithm are required, and is the readable metadata cryptographically bound to the encrypted store?

If the unencrypted record is syntactically readable but has been altered, does Registry trust its instant, release, sequence and key digest for retention and display, or must their authenticity be verified before the file counts as kept?
Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce-generation rule, key derivation or key-size rule, and versioned ciphertext format are required?

What is the exact encoding of this unencrypted record, what ranges and canonical forms are valid, and how is it authenticated so tampering cannot change retention age, release, sequence number or key identity without detection?
Which digest construction and representation identify a backup key, and is it a plain hash, keyed identifier or salted fingerprint?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the backup's authenticated-encryption construction, key identification and container format.

precedent.topic: Backup encryption, key digest, authentication, and container format
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Configuration value syntax, encoding, and secret byte representation or length measurement
questions: Which encodings and syntax make each configuration value well formed, and which byte representation is used for secret length, equality and cryptographic use?
What makes the store location, backup location, owner credential, service tokens and backup key well formed beyond the separately stated presence, path and minimum-length checks?
Environment variables are text; under which encoding is their byte length measured, and are arbitrary non-ASCII or invalidly encoded values accepted?
Beyond minimum secret length and path checks, what exact syntax, encoding and allowed values make each location, credential, token and backup key well formed?
For an environment-variable string, are the 32 bytes counted before decoding, after UTF-8 encoding, or after decoding a declared representation such as hexadecimal or base64?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about configuration-secret encoding, byte counting, equality and representation.

precedent.topic: Byte encoding, length measurement, equality, and comparison of secrets
quotes:
A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at
   least 32 bytes long; a shorter one fails the start.

A presented secret is compared in constant time; no secret enters a record,
   a log line, an audit entry, a diagnostic or an answer (R0-23, R0-37).
precedent.why: The textual or binary representation, decoding, equality and byte-counting rules for credential fields are encoding and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Exact accepted configuration environment-variable names
questions: What are the exact accepted `REGISTRY_` names, so that presence, unknown-item rejection and Unicode-name ordering are deterministic?
What exact environment-variable name corresponds to each required item, and therefore which REGISTRY_-prefixed names are accepted rather than rejected as unknown?
What is the exact environment-variable name for each listed item, so that Registry can distinguish required variables from unknown ones?

quotes:
The configuration is the set of environment variables whose names begin
   with `REGISTRY_`, set as R0-23 says; no other variable is read or
   checked. It holds exactly these items and no other: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four: Registry then serves the owner interface alone
   and refuses every service call (A18 rule 9).
judgement.why: Exact environment-variable names are configuration field names and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Expiry-pass session set, first run, cadence, and handling of delayed or overlapping passes
questions: What is one pass's session set, and are missed or overlapping 60-second passes skipped, queued or run concurrently?
What is "the start", when is the first pass, and after a delayed pass are missed passes skipped, queued, or rescheduled from the delayed pass?

Does the first pass occur at startup or 60 seconds later, are later passes tied to fixed startup-relative ticks or scheduled 60 seconds after completion, and what happens to a tick while an earlier pass is waiting or still running?

quotes:
A session that has reached a limit serves no request from that
   moment; Registry ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its
   uploaded file with it (M11) — when it notices: at the session's next
   request, or at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from
   the start, whichever comes first.
judgement.why: Every request is refused from the same expiry instant regardless of sweep enumeration or delayed-tick policy, so those scheduling choices change only unobservable cleanup timing.

topics.topic: Locking and expiry-decision rules when an ordinary owner request may end a session and drop its upload
questions: Which locks must an ordinary owner request take when its validity check may end the session and drop an uploaded file, and at what locked point is expiry decided?

Must every request to a session acquire the import lock before checking expiry because it might have to drop an upload, or may an ordinary request end the session and change the upload without that lock?

When an ordinary request that normally takes only the session lock discovers that its session has expired, must it first take the import lock before ending the session and dropping a possible upload, and how can it do so without reversing the required lock order?

quotes:
A session that has reached a limit serves no request from that
   moment; Registry ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its
   uploaded file with it (M11) — when it notices: at the session's next
   request, or at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from
   the start, whichever comes first.

The pass takes the import lock and then
   each session's lock (A16 rule 2), and decides under that lock.

An uploaded file is changed only by a holder of the import lock: an
   accepted import, holding it, drops every session's upload; the upload of
   a session ended by its limits goes with the session, when Registry ends it
   (A13 rule 2).

Other
   session changes take their session's lock alone.
judgement.divergence: One implementation acquires the import lock before the session lock whenever an ordinary request may expire its session, while another checks under the session lock and drops the upload without the import lock or must release and retry; concurrent imports, uploads and expiry can consequently complete in different orders or deadlock, which the owner notices as different accepted, refused or stalled requests.
judgement.why: The texts require import-lock protection for changing an upload but do not say how an ordinary request that discovers expiry obtains that lock without reversing the declared lock order.

topics.topic: Audit sequence recorded and checked when the audit history is empty
questions: What last audit sequence is recorded and checked for an empty audit history?
What sequence value is recorded and checked when the store has never written an audit entry?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about representing and validating the last audit sequence for an empty audit history.

precedent.topic: Audit sequence and end-check semantics for an empty audit history
quotes:
It
   records, readable without its key, its instant, the release that made it,
   the last audit sequence number it holds and a digest of the key it was
   made with (never the key); its age is counted from that instant.

Second, it
   writes the backup under a temporary name and checks it: it decrypts it
   into a second temporary file, opens that for reading only, checks that it
   is the store version of its release, that the store's own integrity check
   passes and that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number, and
   removes it; a backup that passes is renamed to its kept name, one that
   fails is deleted.
precedent.why: The empty-log representation of the sequence metadata and its encoded validation rule are field-type and backup-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Backup snapshot point, consistency with live writes, and recorded instant
questions: At what single point is the backup deemed taken, and must both recorded values describe exactly the same snapshot?
What serialization or snapshot rule defines the backup's point in history, and may owner, service, import and audit-erasure transactions continue while the copy is being made?
At what event is the backup's recorded instant fixed: run start, snapshot creation, completion of encryption/checking, or rename to the kept name?

quotes:
A backup is a consistent copy of the store
   taken while Registry runs: it never holds part of a transaction.

It
   records, readable without its key, its instant, the release that made it,
   the last audit sequence number it holds and a digest of the key it was
   made with (never the key); its age is counted from that instant.

Third, whatever the second step did, it deletes every kept
   backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before the instant this step starts,
   one cutoff for the whole step, and every file under the kept
   prefix whose unencrypted record (rule 1) cannot be read.
judgement.divergence: One implementation takes a transactional snapshot while writes continue and records the snapshot instant and its sequence, while another blocks writes through copying or records the instant at completion or rename; callers notice different write latency and the owner notices different backup contents, displayed age and deletion time.
judgement.why: The rules require a consistent backup but leave open its serialization point and when its recorded instant and audit sequence are sampled.

topics.topic: How request arrival is recorded and ordered against session expiry sweeps
questions: If a request arrives before the idle limit but the sweep obtains the session lock after the limit, is validity decided from the arrival instant or from the order in which the request and sweep obtain the lock, and how is the arrival recorded safely against the sweep?
How is an arrival recorded relative to the pass, so that a request which arrived before the idle limit but is still waiting for a lock prevents the pass from ending the session?

quotes:
An owner
   request is any request to the owner interface that
   carries the valid session, whatever its answer; its arrival restarts the 30
   minutes — of concurrent requests the latest arrival counts; before the
   first request it runs from the sign-in.

Validity is
   checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1); a request that
   passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs, and
   a restart that interrupts it leaves nothing of it (A04 rule 4).
judgement.why: Validity and idle renewal are explicitly decided at request arrival, so a request arriving before the limit remains admitted even if a sweep later obtains the lock.

topics.topic: Locking required when an accepted import drops uploads in other sessions
questions: Does an accepted import have to take every affected session's lock before clearing its upload, or is each upload a separately import-lock-protected field that may change while another request holds that session's lock?
When an accepted import drops uploads belonging to other sessions, must it also take every affected session's lock, or is the import lock alone sufficient for those other sessions' upload fields?

quotes:
Uploads
   and every other request that reads or changes an uploaded file — showing
   the mapping or the import's confirmation step, confirming, a sign-out —
   take the instance's one import lock first, then their session's lock
   (A13), check the closure while holding them, and hold both until done;

An uploaded file is changed only by a holder of the import lock: an
   accepted import, holding it, drops every session's upload; the upload of
   a session ended by its limits goes with the session, when Registry ends it
   (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: The import lock already excludes every other operation that can read or change an upload, so additionally taking the other sessions' locks changes only internal waiting and not any specified result.

topics.topic: Validation and supported on-disk format when creating or opening a store
questions: Does starting on an existing store also run the store's integrity check or validate its schema and required invariants, and what exact corruption is sufficient to refuse startup?
What store engine and on-disk format are used, where is the store version recorded, and what exact checks constitute opening it successfully for reading and writing?

quotes:
otherwise
   the store must open for reading and writing and carry the store
   version of the running release, and a store of another version, or one
   that does not open, fails the start — bringing a store to a new version is
   a step of the release, not of the start.

Second, it
   writes the backup under a temporary name and checks it: it decrypts it
   into a second temporary file, opens that for reading only, checks that it
   is the store version of its release, that the store's own integrity check
   passes and that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number, and
   removes it; a backup that passes is renamed to its kept name, one that
   fails is deleted.
judgement.divergence: One implementation starts whenever the existing store opens read-write and has the expected version, while another also runs the store integrity check and refuses a corrupt but openable store; the owner notices Registry serving from that store versus refusing startup.
judgement.why: Although the engine and on-disk encoding belong later, State 2 leaves the consequential startup refusal rule open by requiring an integrity check for backup verification but not saying whether existing live stores receive it.

topics.topic: Backup filename prefixes and canonical instant-to-filename conversion
questions: What are the two prefixes and the exact canonical conversion from an instant to a kept filename, including precision and characters, so collision and ordering behavior are deterministic?

topics.topic: Cleanup and identification of startup probes left by failed starts
questions: Which startup step removes a probe left by an earlier failed start, how is that probe identified, and does cleanup occur during an owner-only start where no backup run will occur?

topics.topic: Crash cleanup and retention-safe handling of decrypted backup-check temporary files
questions: What removes a decrypted temporary store after a crash when Registry restarts owner-only or otherwise never reaches another backup run, and how is that plaintext copy prevented from outliving the backup retention and erasure rules?

topics.topic: Cross-process and restart-safe mutual exclusion for backup runs
questions: What state or lock makes a running backup detectable and prevents overlap, especially across two Registry processes using the same store and backup location or across a restart during a run?

topics.topic: Error precedence when closure and another import-request failure both apply
questions: When the closure exists and the same request also has an invalid file, missing mapping input, stale or wrong confirmation value, or another failure, which refusal is returned and how does this interact with A04's global check order?

topics.topic: Exact store integrity check required when testing a backup
questions: What exact integrity check must the store provide, and which failures or incomplete checks make the backup fail?

topics.topic: Preservation and lookup of old backup keys during key rotation
questions: What must preserve old backup keys until their backups are deleted, and how is the recorded key digest resolved to the correct key during restore?

topics.topic: Rules for relative paths and required store and backup path types
questions: Are relative paths accepted and, if so, against which stable directory are they resolved; and must the store location name a regular file while the backup location names a directory?

topics.topic: Temporary-store filename suffix and collision prevention
questions: What suffix is declared, and how is collision with a legitimate configured store name or another process prevented?

topics.topic: Whether a successful import clears pending confirmations in other owner sessions
questions: Does a successful import proactively clear pending import confirmations in every owner session, or do they remain until submission, expiry, replacement or session end?

topics.topic: Whether an expiry pass holds the import lock for the whole traversal or per session
questions: Does one pass hold the import lock for its entire traversal of all sessions, or release and reacquire it around each individual session?

topics.topic: Whether owner-only mode permits all service tokens to be absent
questions: Does the startup presence check require all four service tokens, or accept their complete absence as owner-only mode?
